Title: The development of the perceptual organization of sound by frequency separation in 5-11-year-old children.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: frequency separation threshold; perception of auditory streams
Evidence_Quote: whether the frequency separation threshold, at which the perception of a mixture of sounds turns from being perceived as one stream to two streams, differs between two groups of school-aged children (ages 5-8 and 9-11 years) and adults

Title: Theory of forward and reverse middle-ear transmission applied to otoacoustic emissions in infant and adult ears.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants through 6 months and adults (prior-study data)
Outcome: forward and reverse middle-ear transmittance levels, infant vs adult
Evidence_Quote: In a previous study, distortion product (DP) OAE input/output (I/O) functions were shown to differ at f2 = 6 kHz in adults compared to infants through 6 months of age.

Title: Intrinsic and extrinsic factors associated with night waking in 9-month-old infants.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Outcome: night waking; time awake at night; frequent waking
Evidence_Quote: This study examined relations between infant night waking and both daytime behaviors reflective of poor behavioral and emotional regulation (intrinsic factors) and parent behaviors that may contribute to infant night waking (extrinsic factors) in 41 infants.

Title: Longitudinal developmental changes in spectral peaks of vowels produced by Japanese infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: spectral resonant peaks of vowels; vowel space expansion
Evidence_Quote: This study aims to investigate when and how the two infants become able to produce categorically separated vowels, and covers the ages of 4 to 60 months in order to provide detailed findings on the developmental process of speech production.

Title: Noise in contemporary neonatal intensive care.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: neonates in two NICUs (sound environment survey)
Stimulus_Type: NICU ambient noise (weekly sound surveys; no presented stimulus)
Outcome: weekly equivalent sound levels (LEQ) and exceedance of AAP/SSG recommendations
Evidence_Quote: Median weekly equivalent sound pressure levels (LEQ) for NICU A ranged from 61 to 63 dB (A weighted), depending on the level of care. NICU B L(EQ) measurements ranged from 55 to 60 dB (A weighted).

Title: Simulating the acquisition of lexical tones from continuous dynamic input.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: tonal categorization; lexical tone acquisition
Evidence_Quote: Across four neural network simulations of lexical tone acquisition, self-organizing maps were trained with continuous speech input of increasing variability.

Title: Distortion product otoacoustic emission suppression tuning and acoustic admittance in human infants: birth through 6 months.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: DPOAE suppression tuning curves; ear-canal admittance/reflectance
Outcome: DPOAE suppression tuning and middle-ear indices vs age
Evidence_Quote: Previous work has reported non-adultlike distortion product otoacoustic emission (DPOAE) suppression in human newborns at f2=6000 Hz, indicating an immaturity in peripheral auditory function.

Title: An articulatory basis for the labial-to-coronal effect: /pata/ seems a more stable articulatory pattern than /tapa/.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: coordination between the jaw, the tongue tip, and the lower lip
Evidence_Quote: This paper investigates the coordination between the jaw, the tongue tip, and the lower lip during repetition with rate increase of labial-to-coronal (L(a)C(o)) consonant-vowel-consonant-vowel disyllables (e.g., /pata/) and coronal-to-labial (C(o)L(a)) ones (e.g., /tapa/) by French speakers.

Title: Call repertoire of infant African elephants: first insights into the early vocal ontogeny.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infant elephants from neonatal to 18 months of age
Outcome: call repertoire; call types
Evidence_Quote: Twelve hundred calls of 11 infant elephants from neonatal to 18 months of age recorded at the Vienna Zoo in Austria and at the Daphne Sheldrick's orphanage at the Nairobi National Park, Kenya were analyzed.

Title: Otoacoustic emissions latency difference between full-term and preterm neonates.
Journal: Hearing research
Outcome: otoacoustic emissions latency; time spans of TEOAE components
Evidence_Quote: Transiently evoked otoacoustic emissions (TEOAEs) were recorded from full-term and preterm neonates.

Title: Click-evoked otoacoustic emissions (CEOAEs) recorded from neonates under 13 hours old using conventional and maximum length sequence (MLS) stimulation.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: newborns 6-13 hours old (57 ears in 37 newborns)
Stimulus_Type: click-evoked otoacoustic emissions, conventional and MLS stimulation
Outcome: CEOAE signal-to-noise ratio and screening pass rates
Evidence_Quote: CEOAEs were recorded in a neonatal ward from 57 ears in 37 newborns ranging from 6 to 13h old, using both conventional (50/s) and high rate (5000/s) MLS averaging.

Title: A comparative study of distortion-product-otoacoustic-emission fine structure in human newborns and adults with normal hearing.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: DPOAE levels; fine structure depth; fine structure spacing
Evidence_Quote: Fine structure characteristics in two groups of ten newborns and young adults with normal hearing sensitivity are compared here.

Title: Age-related changes in sensitivity to native phonotactics in Japanese infants.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: Japanese infants at the ages of 6, 12, and 18 months
Stimulus_Type: nonsense words keetsu; nonsense words keets; nonsense words keet
Outcome: discrimination of nonsense words
Evidence_Quote: Japanese infants at the ages of 6, 12, and 18 months were tested on their ability to discriminate three nonsense words with different phonotactic status: canonical keetsu, noncanonical but possible keets, and noncanonical and impossible keet.

Title: Nonlinear analyses of heart rate variability in normal and growth-restricted fetuses.
Journal: Early human development
Outcome: fetal heart rate (FHR) dynamics; largest Lyapunov exponents; correlation dimension
Evidence_Quote: One hundred nineteen fetal heart rate (FHR) recordings from healthy normal fetuses, and 69 recordings from IUGR fetuses were analyzed.

Title: Maturation of the cortical auditory evoked potential in infants and young children.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 10 newborns (<7 days), 19 toddlers (13-41 months), 20 children (4-6 years), 9 adults (18-45 years)
Stimulus_Type: tones (400 Hz and 3000 Hz) and word token /baed/
Outcome: cortical auditory evoked potential (P1, N1, P2, N2) latency and amplitude by age
Evidence_Quote: CAEPs were obtained in response to low (400 Hz) and high (3000 Hz) tones and to the word token /baed/, all presented at 60 dB HL

Title: Absolute pitch among American and Chinese conservatory students: prevalence differences, and evidence for a speech-related critical period.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: absolute pitch prevalence
Evidence_Quote: This paper reports a substantial difference in the prevalence of absolute pitch in two normal populations, in a large-scale study employing an on-site test, without self-selection from within the target populations.

Title: Fundamental frequency of infants' and parents' utterances in longitudinal recordings.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: from the infant's birth until about 5 years of age
Outcome: fundamental frequency (F0)
Evidence_Quote: The fundamental frequencies (F0) of daily life utterances of Japanese infants and their parents from the infant's birth until about 5 years of age were longitudinally analyzed.

Title: Do former preterm infants remember and respond to neonatal intensive care unit noise?
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: former preterm and term infants at 4-5 months corrected age
Outcome: heart rate
Evidence_Quote: To compare the heart rate responses of former preterm and term infants at 4-5 months corrected age to a recording of NICU noises.

Title: A retrospective study of the spectral probability of spontaneous otoacoustic emissions: rise of octave shifted second mode after infancy.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: 296 human subjects: neonates, children (5-11 years), adults
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (recorded; no presented stimulus)
Outcome: SOAE frequency distribution peaks by age group
Evidence_Quote: Neonates show a monomodal distribution with a peak at 4 kHz, but both children (5-11 y) and adults show an identical bimodal distribution, with two peaks in an octave distance (1.5 and 3 kHz).

Title: Acute centralization of blood flow in compromised human fetuses evoked by uterine contractions.
Journal: Early human development
Stimulus_Type: uterine contractions during an oxytocin challenge test
Outcome: middle cerebral artery pulsatility index; umbilical artery pulsatility index
Evidence_Quote: To explore acute fetal middle cerebral artery (MCA) circulatory changes relative to umbilical artery (UA) blood flow in a clinical experimental model with hypoxic stress provoked by uterine contractions during an oxytocin challenge test (OCT).

Title: Effect of masker-frequency variability on the detection performance of infants and adults.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: 1000-Hz pure tone signal with two-tone complex and broadband noise maskers
Outcome: masked detection thresholds by masker condition
Evidence_Quote: Listeners detected a 300-ms 1000-Hz pure tone masked by: (1) A random-frequency two-tone complex; (2) a fixed-frequency two-tone complex; or (3) a broadband noise. Maskers repeated at 300-ms intervals throughout testing at 60 dB SPL.
